skill.name: email-segmentation-specialist
skill.description: Design, audit, and preview email audience segments using consent, lifecycle, interests, behavior, and purchase signals across email providers. Use for segment logic, audience overlap, signup routing, or lifecycle targeting, not permission to send campaigns or upload contacts.
skill.summary: Design consent-aware email segments with explicit audience rules, overlap policies, validation cases, and provider mappings.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

security_audit.summary: The system reconnaissance finding is a false positive: SKILL.md:20 prohibits sensitive-trait inference and unauthorized customer-data transfers. No evidence found of malicious reconnaissance, credential theft, exfiltration instructions, or prompt injection in the reviewed files. The skill distinguishes planning from external changes and requires authorization before implementation.

static_findings.snippet: Never manufacture or infer sensitive traits from browsing, names or purchases to target people. Pref

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md:20 prohibits inferring sensitive traits, minimizes exports, and forbids unauthorized customer-data transfers. This is a privacy safeguard, not an instruction to inspect systems or collect secrets.

content.value_statement: Unclear audience rules can create overlapping campaigns, unreliable reach estimates, and consent errors. This skill defines eligibility gates, segment logic, provider mappings, and validation checks before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Define marketing eligibility gates covering permission, unsubscribe, complaints, hard bounces, and provider suppression.
Specify Boolean audience rules, observation windows, null handling, lifecycle transitions, and segment ownership.
Design lifecycle and declared-interest audiences with explicit entry, exit, priority, and overlap policies.
Guide provider field mapping and identify filters or implementation details requiring verification.
Plan read-only previews and edge-case checks for permission conflicts, time boundaries, duplicate events, and overlapping audiences.
Define downstream outcomes, measurement guardrails, and holdout comparisons without claiming causal uplift from correlations.
limitations: Audience counts and results require authorized data or aggregate counts; missing values remain explicitly unknown.
Provider-specific filters, interfaces, and API support require current documentation or connected-account verification.
Planning does not authorize contact uploads, subscription changes, saved segments, campaign activation, or recurring work.
The skill does not certify legal compliance, infer sensitive traits, or guarantee campaign performance.

use_cases.title: Plan Distinct Lifecycle Audiences
use_cases.description: Define welcome, prospect, customer, and re-engagement segments with clear transitions, consent gates, and campaign priorities.

use_cases.title: Audit Audience Eligibility and Overlap
use_cases.description: Review existing segment rules for suppression gaps, ambiguous permissions, duplicate reach, and missing edge-case tests.

use_cases.title: Design Interest-Based Signup Routing
use_cases.description: Connect declared signup interests to relevant audiences while preserving subscription promises and the chosen email provider.

prompt_templates.title: Propose Starter Segments
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose email segments for [business] and [campaign goal]. Available fields are [fields]. Identify missing eligibility information and keep audience sizes unknown without data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: plan audiences without connected customer data.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a Lifecycle Segment
prompt_templates.prompt: Define a [lifecycle stage] segment using [anonymized schema]. Include permission gates, Boolean rules, time boundaries, null handling, entry, exit, and a next message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: convert a campaign goal into explicit audience rules.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Audience Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [segment definitions] using [aggregate preview counts]. Check suppression gates, permission conflicts, overlap, unique reach, event duplication, and conversion exits. Recommend tests without changing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess audience safety and preview quality before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Provider Implementation Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Map [canonical segment rules] to [provider] using [verified documentation or account schema]. Document unsupported logic, priority, frequency caps, validation cases, and measurement. Do not save or activate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a provider-specific implementation for separate authorization.

output_examples.input: Design a synthetic education-interest prospect audience. Available fields include verified marketing permission, suppression status, declared interests, and verified customer state.
output: State: proposed design, not saved or activated.
Eligibility: verified marketing permission for this sender and purpose, with no unsubscribe, complaint, hard bounce, or provider suppression.
Audience: eligibility AND (declared interests include education) AND (verified customer state equals prospect).
Unknown permission, suppression, interest, or customer state: exclude pending review.
Exit: conversion to customer, interest removal, permission revocation, or suppression.
Overlap: one recipient per campaign, subject to an account-wide frequency cap.
Audience size: unknown until an authorized preview is available.

output_examples.input: For a synthetic preview, segment A has 120 eligible contacts, segment B has 90, and their overlap contains 30. Assess reach and readiness.
output: Unique eligible reach: 180 contacts, calculated as 120 plus 90 minus 30.
The combined segment sizes total 210 memberships, not 210 unique recipients.
The 30 overlapping contacts require campaign deduplication and an explicit message-priority policy.
Send readiness remains unverified until suppression enforcement, frequency limits, onboarding priority, and campaign timing are checked.
State: preview assessment only; no campaign changes are authorized.

best_practices: Place permission and suppression checks outside every audience-specific OR group, and recheck eligibility before sending.
Use anonymized schemas or aggregate counts when sufficient, and document null handling, data freshness, and time boundaries.
Preview edge cases and reconcile unique reach before requesting separate authorization for provider changes.
anti_patterns: Treating purchases, inferred interests, or an email address as marketing permission.
Summing overlapping segment sizes as unique reach or treating missing tracking as confirmed inactivity.
Uploading contacts, changing subscription states, or activating campaigns based only on a planning request.

faq.question: Does this skill send campaigns automatically?
faq.answer: No. A strategy or preview request does not authorize sending, uploads, subscription changes, or saved segments.

faq.question: Do I need to use Poptin?
faq.answer: No. The skill works with your existing provider. Poptin guidance is optional when relevant to lead capture or audience organization.

faq.question: Can I start without customer records?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide your goal and an anonymized field schema. The skill can propose rules while leaving audience sizes and results unknown.

faq.question: How does it handle missing or conflicting consent?
faq.answer: Records with unknown or contradictory permission go to review, not the send audience. Suppression states must remain enforced.

faq.question: Will the proposed rules work in every email platform?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Exact filters and nested logic require verification against current provider documentation or your connected account.

faq.question: Does it guarantee compliance or campaign uplift?
faq.answer: No. Legal questions require current authoritative guidance, and performance claims require appropriate measurements rather than audience correlations.
